quote.translation: Piéron accordingly holds that "subjective interest" (intérêt subjectif) forms an important moment in chance, and he emphasises the "subjective side" (côté subjectif) or "human element" (élément humain) of the phenomenon of chance, a view of interest as the theory of a psychologist (Revue de Métaphysique et de Morale, 1902, p. 688-691).

regions.text: あるものである（RevuedeMetaphysiqueetdeMorale,1902,p688-691）なほ偶然の心理的解釋に屬するものとして原因に於ける徹小の差異が、若果に於て大きい差異を衛すものが偶然であるといふ考がある。

quote.translation: Also belonging to the psychological interpretation of chance is the idea that chance is that in which a minute difference in the cause brings about a large difference in the effect.

quote.translation: Renan, for example, says that chance is "what does not have a moral cause proportioned to the effect" (ce qui n'a pas de cause morale proportionnée à l'effet) (Ernest Renan, L'Avenir de la Science, p. 24), and Poincaré too says of chance that "the difference in the cause is imperceptible, and the difference in the effect is for me of very great importance" (La différence dans la cause est imperceptible, et la différence dans l'effet est pour moi de la plus haute importance) (H. Poincaré, Science et Méthode, p. 71).

quote.translation: When we judge an effect to be large in comparison with its cause, the standard of that evaluation lies mainly in purposiveness, and consequently the so-called "grave effect" often turns out to be nothing other than a "purpose without purpose".

regions.text: 重大なる結果の例として、ルナンが『リュツェンで砲弾に中つたグスターフアドルフ」（Cマ袋）を擧げ、ポアンカレが「戦慄すべき災害」（TCPこ）を暴げてるるのに照しても明かである。

quote.translation: This is clear from the examples of grave effects that the two give: Renan cites "Gustavus Adolphus struck by a cannonball at Lützen" (l. c. p. 494) and Poincaré "a terrible catastrophe" (l. c. p. 68).

regions.text: またルナンが特に『精神約」と云い、ボアンカレが「私にとつて」と云つでゐるのもそのためである。

quote.translation: It is for the same reason that Renan specifies a "moral" cause and Poincaré says "for me".
